items.item_text: Possess and maintain a valid California Class B driver’s license (Class B CDL) with air brake and passenger endorsements.
Possess and maintain a valid California Class C driver’s license
Able to obtain and maintain a current medical certificate in compliance with DMV/DOT requirements.
BLS/CPR from American Red Cross or American Heart Association within 6 months of hire.
Ability to participate in safety training/certification programs.
High School Diploma or equivalent
One (1) year of professional commercial vehicle driving experience.

Under the general supervision of the Education Manager, the EHS Mobile Unit Driver provides safe, reliable, and professional transportation services to support children, families, staff, and community partners participating in Early Head Start and Head Start programs. The position operates a variety of vehicles, conducts required safety inspections, maintains transportation records and compliance documentation, and ensures adherence to all transportation regulations and program standards. The Driver also supports program operations by transporting materials and donations, assisting with the Mobile Classroom Unit, participating in training and community collaborations, and helping ensure families have access to essential program services through high-quality customer service and safe transportation practices.
Work Locations: East San Fernando Valley- including but not limited to Arleta, Pacoima, Sylmar, Lake View Terrace, etc.
This is a limited position that may convert to career.
Driving Record: The position is subject to the California DMV "Pull Notice System" and continued employment is contingent upon proof of a satisfactory driving record.

Per funding agency requirements, all Early Head Start staff must complete background checks before first day of hire, and at least every five years that includes, sex offender registry check, State or FBI criminal history check, including fingerprint check, child abuse registry check.
Must meet state health requirements that include passing a physical examination as condition of employment, providing verification of COVID-19 vaccine, TB Clearance, and up to date with immunization.
Knowledge of driving laws as specified in the California Vehicle Code. Skill in the safe operation of various passenger vehicles to provide transportation as directed.

Ability to communicate effectively and maintain tactful, professional relationships with families, Early Head Start staff, supervisors, passengers, co-workers, community resource agencies, consultants, and volunteers, including relaying information to passengers politely, clearly, and effectively to support families in locating and accessing appropriate community services as needed.
Ability to maintain accurate, legible logs and records.
Ability to use Push-To-Talk (PTT) radio and/or cellular phone for communication purposes.

Ability to handle complex procedures on CNG vehicle fueling, fuel monitoring, use wheelchair lifts, ramps and other special equipment. Ability to detect irregular vehicle performance to recognize required maintenance or repairs.
Ability to use mapping tools such as GPS System, MapQuest, Google Maps and Thomas Guide for selecting event routing.
Ability to maintain excellent attendance and punctuality to meet specific deadlines. Ability to work extended hours, when needed to meet all departmental responsibilities.
Ability to work in an environment with occasional exposure to dust, gases, fumes, chemicals, loud noise levels, changes in temperature while or during operating a motor vehicle.

Required Physical Abilities: Ability to carry children, up to 50 pounds during each workday when necessary. Ability to engage in frequent bending, reaching, twisting and engage in moderate to frequent kneeling, crawling, and stooping while observing, or performing classroom activities. Ability to engage in frequent writing, typing on keyboards, and handling small objects (e.g. arts and crafts for children). Ability to sit or stand for prolonged periods of time that may exceed an hour at a time. This includes sitting on the floor for extended periods (e.g. while engaging in child development activities during home visit, classroom, and socialization sessions).
